gloss: inevitably; willy-nilly; like it or not

definitions.gloss: inevitably; willy-nilly; whether one likes it or not
definitions.explanation: Describes something that happens regardless of one's wishes or consent. Indicates that there is no choice in the matter—it will happen whether you want it to or not.

examples.japanese: {否応|いやおう}なく⟦{決断|けつだん}→決断：13250_ketsudan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迫|せま}られた→迫る：03928_semaru⟧。
examples.english: I was forced to make a decision whether I liked it or not.

examples.japanese: ⟦グローバル→グローバル：10847_guroobaru⟧⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{否応|いやおう}なく⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: With globalization, English became inevitably necessary.

examples.japanese: ⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{流|なが}れ→流れ：03504_nagare⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{否応|いやおう}なく⟦{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる→巻き込む：05753_makikomu⟧。
examples.english: One gets swept up in the currents of the times, like it or not.

notes:
FORMS:
{否|いや} (no, refusal) + {応|おう} (yes, consent) + なく (without)
Literally "without a yes or a no" — that is, without asking whether you agree.
- {否応|いやおう}なく - the standard adverbial form
- {否応|いやおう}⟦なし→無し：03779_nashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ - same meaning, slightly more emphatic and a little more literary
- ⟦{有無|うむ}→有無：13019_umu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}わさず→言う：00515_iu⟧ - without letting anyone object; stresses an agent overriding you, where {否応|いやおう}なく usually points at circumstances

USAGE:
{否応|いやおう}なく modifies a verb, and that verb is nearly always one of being acted upon — a passive, or a change that happens to the subject:
- {否応|いやおう}なく⟦{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる→巻き込む：05753_makikomu⟧ (to be drawn in regardless)
- {否応|いやおう}なく⟦{従|したが}う→従う：02059_shitagau⟧ (to comply whether one likes it or not)
- {否応|いやおう}なく⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧ (to change inevitably)
It is not used of things the subject chose to do, so 否応なく行った sounds wrong unless the going was imposed.
The force is external — social change, an employer, the passage of time — and the speaker's own preference has been bypassed rather than overruled in argument. It is common in writing about society and history, and carries a note of resignation.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{必然|ひつぜん}→必然：05533_hitsuzen⟧ - inevitability as a logical outcome; states that something had to follow, without the sense of a will being ignored
